events.title: The Third Council of Constantinople opens in the imperial palace
events.description: Only 37 bishops and several presbyters met in the Trullus, a domed hall of the imperial palace, to open the Third Council of Constantinople. By its close in 681 it had condemned monoenergism and monothelitism as heresies.

events.title: Charles the Simple and Henry the Fowler sign the Treaty of Bonn
events.description: Charles the Simple, king of West Francia, and Henry the Fowler, king of East Francia, signed a "pact of friendship" aboard a ship in the middle of the Rhine near Bonn. The river was the border between their kingdoms.
events.html: Charles the Simple, king of West Francia, and Henry the Fowler, king of East Francia, signed a "pact of friendship" aboard a ship in the middle of the Rhine near Bonn. The river was the border between their kingdoms.

events.title: Lam Sơn rebels ambush and rout a Ming army near Hanoi
events.description: Armed with hand cannons, Vietnamese rebels under Lê Lợi ambushed and routed a Ming army under General Wang Tong between the villages of Tốt Động and Chúc Động, near Hanoi. It was the decisive battle of the Lam Sơn uprising.

events.title: The Ensisheim meteorite falls in Alsace
events.description: A stony meteorite fell in a wheat field outside the walled town of Ensisheim in Alsace. It is the oldest recorded meteorite fall in Europe whose stone survives, and it can still be seen in the town's museum.

events.title: The Oxford Gazette, later the London Gazette, is first published
events.description: With the court in Oxford to escape the plague, the first issue of the Oxford Gazette appeared. Renamed the London Gazette, it is the oldest continuously published newspaper in Britain.
events.html: With the court in Oxford to escape the plague, the first issue of the Oxford Gazette appeared. Renamed the London Gazette, it is the oldest continuously published newspaper in Britain.

events.title: A pro-slavery mob kills Elijah Lovejoy
events.description: The abolitionist editor Elijah Lovejoy was shot defending his fourth printing press from a mob in Alton, Illinois. His death turned many northerners towards the anti-slavery cause.
events.html: The abolitionist editor Elijah Lovejoy was shot defending his fourth printing press from a mob in Alton, Illinois. His death turned many northerners towards the anti-slavery cause.

events.title: Marie Curie is born in Warsaw
events.description: Maria Skłodowska was born in Warsaw, then under Russian rule. As Marie Curie she pioneered research on radioactivity and became the first person to win Nobel Prizes in two sciences.
events.html: Maria Skłodowska was born in Warsaw, then under Russian rule. As Marie Curie she pioneered research on radioactivity and became the first person to win Nobel Prizes in two sciences.

events.title: The Bolsheviks seize power in Petrograd
events.description: Bolshevik-led Red Guards took key points in Petrograd and stormed the Winter Palace overnight, toppling the Provisional Government. The October Revolution, so called from the Julian calendar, led to the Soviet state.

events.title: The Tacoma Narrows Bridge collapses
events.description: Four months after opening, the suspension bridge over Puget Sound twisted violently in a 40-mile-per-hour wind and fell into the water. Filmed footage of 'Galloping Gertie' transformed bridge aerodynamics.
